top_priority_shootable_angles.hook: Turn this creator topic into a safe question: Eating a large amount of sunflower seed shells can do more than just upset your stomach. The shells are mostly made of rough, indigestible fiber, so instead of breaking down, they can clump together, dry out, and form a painful fecal impaction. On the way out, those sharp shell fragments can also scrape the rectum and anus, causing pain, bleeding, and small tears. In other words, eat the seed, not the shell. #ERdoctor #ConstipationRelief #DigestiveHealth #MedicalFacts

top_priority_shootable_angles.hook: Turn this creator topic into a safe question: Peas are a gut-health MVP: they bring fiber that helps keep digestion moving, plus prebiotic fibers that feed your beneficial gut bacteria. They also contain resistant starch and fermentable carbs that can support a healthier microbiome. And here’s what makes them even more valuable—those fermentable fibers get broken down by your gut microbes into short-chain fatty acids like butyrate, which help nourish your gut lining, reduce inflammation, and support overall gut function. On top of that, peas provide plant-based protein and polyphenols that further support microbial diversity and metabolic health. #plantbased #healthyfood #easyrecipes #fiber
